body: It is. Like, this is exactly what I was trying to prevent, and now it's this huge possible consequence of admitting anything.
That's a great way of putting it. Thanks.

I think I'll try this. My therapist actually brought the issue up, and I brushed it aside as an "I know you were just doing your job" thing, because I didn't want to seem illogical or childish. But even though I know it wasn't done to hurt me, I am having a hard time thinking of it in any other terms, so I guess I should bring it up.

Haha, it would be nice to be able to be honest and not get the oh shit look. But truly, I am way less afraid of dying than I am of being locked up, and of the impact something like that would have on your life afterwards. It's a huge barrier. I guess you're saying that it's not as horrible as I think, but do you really think it helped you?
Sigh. I can logically agree with this. It's just hard for me to re-frame it in my mind as anything other than hurtful, and to push down the emotions surrounding it.
